results.title: Battery Pack Tariffs: What OEMs Need to Know in 2026
results.content:
Battery pack tariffs changed the rules overnight. Tariffs that OEM engineers and procurement managers once treated as background noise have become the single most disruptive force in US battery pack sourcing. Since January 2025, the cost of importing battery components from China has risen by as much as 69 percent. For manufacturers who built their supply chains around offshore pricing, the math no longer works. [...] Multiple tariff measures took effect simultaneously. A 93.5 percent tariff on Chinese graphite – the primary anode material in virtually all lithium-ion batteries – took effect, representing one of the most significant raw material tariffs in US manufacturing history. A 30 percent baseline tariff on all Chinese goods compounded the impact on battery cells and pack components sourced from China. Steel and copper tariffs of 50 percent added further cost pressure on pack housings, connectors, [...] Key Context: The Supreme Court struck down tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) in February 2026, but the administration continued pursuing battery-related trade barriers through other legal authorities including Section 232 investigations, while maintaining existing measures including a 10 percent import surcharge under Section 122. The regulatory environment remains fluid.
